# Skeleton

The shape of content that has not arrived. Used only where the shape is known; where it is not, say so in words instead.

## Anatomy

One or more blocks, the last of a multi-line set shortened, pulsing slowly.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | `'text' \| 'label' \| 'block'` | `'text', width = '100%', height, lines = 1` | `text` matches a body line, `label` a mono micro-label, `block` an arbitrary box. |
| `width` | `string` | — | CSS width. A skeleton stands in for content whose width is not known. |
| `height` | `string` | — | — |
| `lines` | `number` | — | — |

## Variants

`text` matches a body line, `label` a mono micro-label, `block` an arbitrary box.

## States

Static, pulsing; stilled under reduced motion.

## Keyboard

Not interactive.

## ARIA

`aria-hidden`. A screen reader gains nothing from the shape of a wait — the surface announces the wait through its own live region.

## Accessibility acceptance criteria

- Reachable, operable and leavable by keyboard alone, with a focus indicator meeting 3:1 in both schemes.
- An accessible name for every control, and current state exposed programmatically.
- No meaning carried by colour alone.
- Legible and operable at a 360px viewport and at desktop width, and at 200% zoom.
- Interactive targets at least 44 × 44px on touch-capable viewports.

## Reference correspondence

None. The reference has no loading state at all. The blocks take the sunken surface its filled fields use.

## Recorded deviations

None.
